position: CFTC Administration and Improved Commodities and Derivatives Markets
proposal: The Mandate recommends that Congress clarify by amending the Commodity Exchange Act when a foreign swap trading platform must register as a swap execution facility. It also recommends that the CFTC apply the 2020 cross-border rule's U.S. person and guarantee definitions to requirements still under the 2013 guidance, and drop the affiliate conduit and foreign consolidated subsidiary categories.

sources.title: CFTC harmonizes U.S. person and guarantee definitions in swap requirements
US CFTC staff issues no-action relief to simplify cross-border swaps regulation

status_summary: On 2025-12-09 three CFTC divisions issued staff no-action letter 25-42, under which staff will not recommend enforcement if market participants classify counterparties using the 2020 cross-border rule's U.S. person and guarantee definitions for the clearing, trade execution and reporting requirements still covered by the 2013 guidance and for uncleared swap margin, and if they disregard non-U.S. conduit affiliates; the letter applies until the Commission adopts rules, is not binding on the Commission and can be modified or withdrawn by staff. A staff letter of 2026-03-24 (26-10) added two UK swap trading facilities to an earlier staff letter tied to SEF registration, an exemption route rather than the statutory clarification the Mandate asks Congress to enact. The letter does not mention the foreign consolidated subsidiary category, and no Commission rule or bill on these items was found.

timeline.event: CFTC staff issued no-action letter 25-42 allowing use of the 2020 rule's U.S. person and guarantee definitions for requirements still under the 2013 guidance and for uncleared margin, and disregard of non-U.S. conduit affiliates, until the Commission adopts rules.

CFTC Division of Market Oversight issued staff letter 26-10 adding two UK facilities (OptAxe Limited and Capitolis UK Limited) to the appendix of staff letter 24-11, under which staff will not recommend enforcement for failure to register as a SEF under CEA section 5h(a)(1) and Regulation 37.3(a)(1) or against counterparties using those facilities under the trade execution requirement.

title: Harmonize CFTC cross-border swap definitions and clarify foreign platform SEF registration
uncertainties: Letter 25-42 was re-read in this review on cftc.gov in summary form; it gives no separate relief on the foreign consolidated subsidiary category, and whether applying the 2020 definitions to uncleared margin displaces that concept in practice is not stated and is not assumed. It also allows reliance on pre-2020 representations for Group B and Group C requirements, supersedes inconsistent cross-references in letters 20-18, 20-21, 21-09 and 25-16, and applies before and after 2027-12-31 until the Commission adopts rules. Letter 26-10 was read in full by the researcher on cftc.gov. The 2026-07-17 uncleared margin rule (91 FR 45134), read in full by the researcher, concerns seeded funds and money market fund collateral and has no cross-border content, so it was removed from the sources. Staff relief is treated as partly operative but not as the Commission action the Mandate asks for, so the record is in_progress rather than implemented; implemented 65 is defensible. Bills on SEF registration were not searched; no Commission rulemaking on these items was found in the sources read.
